text.en: Believing a nuclear isomer is a chemically or physically distinct element or substance from the ground-state nucleus of the same isotope -- an isomer has exactly the same number of protons and neutrons as the ground-state nucleus and is therefore chemically identical to it in every respect; the only difference is that the isomer's nucleus is trapped in a higher-energy internal configuration, giving it its own distinct half-life, decay mode, and often distinct nuclear spin, properties that are entirely internal to the nucleus rather than anything a chemist could detect by ordinary chemical means.
text.et: Arvamus, et tuumaisomeer on keemiliselt või füüsikaliselt erinev element või aine sama isotoobi põhiolekus olevast tuumast -- isomeeril on täpselt sama arv prootoneid ja neutroneid kui põhiolekus oleval tuumal ning see on seetõttu sellega keemiliselt identne igas mõttes; ainus erinevus on see, et isomeeri tuum on lõksus kõrgema energiaga sisemises konfiguratsioonis, andes sellele oma eraldiseisva poolestusaja, lagunemisviisi ja sageli eraldiseisva tuuma spinni, omadused, mis on täielikult tuuma sisemised, mitte midagi, mida keemik saaks tavaliste keemiliste vahenditega tuvastada.
